resolutions.researcher_notes: DNR Minstroy Order 58-od (27 Mar 2025) repeatedly refers to the object as a 'магистральный газопровод' (trunk GAS pipeline) at each of its three named stretches, including the Taganrog-Mariupol one on this row.
Same decree describes it as 'магистральный' (trunk/main-line), which is GEM's 'transmission' class, not a gathering/distribution line.

Two independent origins agree on both endpoints: the DNR decree names the route 'Таганрог-Мариуполь' explicitly (Taganrog, Rostov Oblast, Russia -> Mariupol, Donetsk, Ukraine), and Ukrainian outlet United24 independently reports Russia building a pipeline 'from Taganrog, Russia, to the occupied Mariupol.'

DNR Minstroy Order 58-od (27.03.2025), OCR text read directly from the item's own djvu.txt derivative, repeatedly names this object 'magistralnogo gazoprovoda Mariupol-Berdyansk Du500' (main GAS pipeline) -- direct textual support for Fuel=Gas. Item page itself is live (url_verifier passes on '58-od' / '27.03.2025'); substring probes for Cyrillic 'gazoprovod'/'Berdyansk' fail against the bare details-page metadata (title/description only run a few words), which is expected for an archive.org item landing page -- I confirmed the actual content via the item's own full-text derivative, per url_verifier.py's documented content-false-negative guidance.

Same order explicitly calls this a 'magistralny gazoprovod' -- 'magistralny' = main/trunk transmission line (the standard Russian/Soviet technical term distinguishing trunk pipelines from distribution/gathering lines), supporting PipelineType=transmission (consistent with its parent P1457 original trunk and sibling P7817).

Order text names the object 'Mariupol-Berdyansk' verbatim, directly naming both endpoint cities. Oblast attribution (Donetsk / Zaporizhzhia) is standard geography, not separately sourced by this document.

Searched Russian and Ukrainian sources for anything newer than the sheet's 10 Oct 2025 LastUpdated / 27 Mar 2025 decree: tsoua.com (no mention -- this segment is occupied territory, outside TSOU's actual network), DAN/TASS/mytaganrog.com/mariupol local news, and general 2026 Mariupol gas-utility news. Found a DNR Ministry of Property and Land Relations notice dated 23 Jun 2025 seeking a 49-year public easement for the SAME three repair objects named in the March decree (verbatim identical route/diameter language) -- this pushes the most recent dated, project-specific evidence to June 2025 and shows the project was still in a land-acquisition/administrative phase then, not yet complete. No source (Ukrainian, Russian, or trade press) reports this specific segment as finished/commissioned. 2026 Mariupol gas-utility news (Донбассгаз/ЧМНГ) covers routine local distribution maintenance, not this trunk repair. Given no completion evidence and no independent report contradicting 'construction', I confirm the recorded Status. The dormancy/staleness rules (2y->shelved, 4y->cancelled) apply to 'proposed'/'shelved' rows, not 'construction', so they aren't triggered here regardless.

Newest segment-specific evidence is the DNR Minstroy order (27.03.2025): planning documentation approved for a 0.3 km capital-repair stretch of Mariupol-Berdyansk -- i.e. still at the documentation/approval stage, not physical construction, consistent with Status=proposed. Independent (Ukrainian) corroboration that pipeline construction activity continues generally along this Taganrog-Mariupol-Berdyansk-Melitopol corridor comes from united24media.com (24 Jul 2025, verified), though that article is about the corridor broadly and does not confirm or deny progress on the Mariupol-Berdyansk stretch specifically. Searched (RU/EN, Aug 2026) for any 2026 progress report specific to 'Mariupol-Berdyansk' capital repair / construction start -- found nothing newer than the 2025-03 order; TASS's 2024-04-29 piece on the 'Taganrog-Melitopol' modernization (P5989) discusses the DNR-side (Taganrog-Mariupol) segment and Zaporizhzhia-wide supply, not this specific Mariupol-Berdyansk stretch. Two Russian-origin items (the DNR order and the TASS/dan-news items on the neighboring corridor) count as ONE origin per the country brief; United24 is the second, independent origin, but it corroborates the corridor generally rather than this segment's exact status. Evidence age (~13-17 months as of Aug 2026) is well under the 2-year 'proposed with no progress' dormancy threshold, so 'confirm' rather than 'stale' is the right call -- but see the duplicate flag above: if P5989 is later found to already cover this exact stretch as 'operating,' this status would need revisiting as part of that adjudication, not as an independent status change here.

resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE + CLASSIFICATION: real, and correctly distinguished from its GEM neighbors. The sheet's own DNR Minstroy Order No. 58-od (27 Mar 2025, archive.org/details/58_20251012) is a primary occupation-administration planning decree that approves siting documentation for 'капитальный ремонт магистрального газопровода Таганрог-Мариуполь [1-я нитка] Ду700 на участке 29,0-71,625 км методом замены трубы' (capital repair / pipe-replacement of the Taganrog-Mariupol trunk gas pipeline, DN700, on the 29.0-71.625 km stretch) -- this independently confirms PipelineName, route (Taganrog RU -> Mariupol UA), Diameter=700mm, Fuel=Gas, PipelineType=transmission ('магистральный'), and that GEM's own SegmentName 'Reconstructed Segment' is the right characterization (this is a REBUILD of a pre-existing Soviet line, not new-build). Found a second DNR document repeating the identical route/diameter language: DNR Ministry of Property and Land Relations public-easement notice dated 23 June 2025 (mariupol-news.ru/politics/2025/06/23/116808.html, verified) -- but this is the SAME origin bucket as the Minstroy decree (both DNR occupation administration), so per country guidance it counts as ONE source, not two. The second, genuinely independent leg is the sheet's other existing ref, United24 (Ukrainian, 24 Jul 2025 dateline citing a 16 Jul 2024 tweet by the Center for Journalistic Investigations with satellite/drone footage) reporting Russia 'laying two pipelines simultaneously -- one from Taganrog...to...Mariupol, and another continuing to Berdyansk, with Melitopol as the final destination.' CAVEAT: I read the full United24 article and it never actually uses the word 'gas' -- it calls them generically 'pipelines' in the context of a broader Rostov-to-Crimea 'land corridor' (which also covers a parallel railway project). The route match to the DNR decree's gas-pipeline corridor is very tight (identical city sequence, identical construction-year window) so I still count it as a second independent origin for EXISTENCE/STATUS, but it is not itself proof the pipelines shown in that footage are the gas line rather than some other utility/rail corridor -- worth knowing before leaning on it further. DUPLICATE CHECK (against the wider Taganrog family, none of it a false duplicate): P1457 (same PipelineName, same Wiki page, status=retired, Taganrog->Berdyansk, LengthKnownKm=516, Diameter=1000mm) is the ORIGINAL big trunk that this row's SegmentName says is being reconstructed -- correctly kept as a separate retired row, not merged with P7817/P7818. P5989 ('Taganrog-Melitopol-Berdyansk Gas Pipeline', status=operating since 2024, Taganrog->Melitopol, LengthEstimateKm=272.73) is a DIFFERENT, already-completed bypass pipeline that skips Mariupol entirely (built instead of reviving the old Mariupol route, per gem.wiki's own background on that page) -- different endpoints, different length order of magnitude, sourced from TASS/DAN only (one Russian-state origin, correctly not elevated). None of these should be folded into P7817; they are three distinct, correctly-separated entities sharing one Soviet-era corridor. ATTRIBUTION: Owner is blank on the sheet. A 2014 Neftegaz.ru piece describes the ORIGINAL (pre-2009) pipeline as 'belonging to Gazprom' historically, but I found no 2024/2025-dated source naming a current owner/operator for the reconstruction (the Minstroy decree only names the planning-documentation contractor, OOO 'Tsentr kompleksnogo proektirovaniya', which is a design consultancy, not an asset owner). Per country guidance I am not filling Owner with Gazprom off a 12-year-old pre-closure fact for occupied Ukrainian territory -- leaving it blank with this note rather than fabricate a current attribution.

resolutions.recommendation: Re-derive Length for this segment from a route-specific figure rather than the current straight-line city-to-city estimate; flag LengthEstimateKm=104.50 as likely overstated pending a sourced route length.
resolutions.researcher_notes: LengthEstimateKm=104.50 / LengthMergedKm=104.50 on the sheet is not sourced (LengthKnownKm is blank) -- it reads as an auto-computed geodesic distance between the Taganrog and Mariupol city points (straight-line Taganrog-Mariupol is ~103-104 km, matching the figure almost exactly). But the only documented physical length I could find for THIS specific local pipe is much shorter: a 22 Oct 2014 Neftegaz.ru article (verified) quotes then-DNR fuel/energy minister A. Granovsky describing 'the 33-kilometer main gas pipeline (MGP) "Taganrog-Mariupol", built in the 1950s and closed in 2009 after the Russia-Ukraine gas conflict,' and separately quotes a 2014 Gazprom liquidation tender for the object 'Магистральный газопровод Таганрог-Мариуполь 1 нитка 20,4-56,7 км' (i.e. km-marker range 20.4-56.7, a 36.3 km stretch). The 2025 DNR Minstroy decree's own repair-section markers (km 29.0-71.625, a 42.6 km stretch) are in the same rough range and clearly NOT measured from a Taganrog-city zero point -- they look like markers along a longer trunk (consistent with the wiki page's own title, 'Rostov-Taganrog-Zhdanov', i.e. a route that may start further away at Rostov, which is what P1457's separate 516 km/1000mm figure may actually represent). Either way, none of the historical/documentary evidence supports a ~104.5 km figure specifically for the Taganrog-Mariupol reconstructed segment; the true figure is more likely in the 33-57 km band. I did not find a single authoritative total-length figure I'd stake a fill on, so I'm flagging this as a concern rather than proposing a replacement number -- someone should look at whether LengthEstimateKm should be suppressed/replaced once a real route source is available (e.g. via a §8 route-creation pass).

resolutions.recommendation: Cluster-level adjudication: compare P7818 (+ P7817) against P5989 'Taganrog-Melitopol-Berdyansk Gas Pipeline' (OtherEnglishNames 'Taganrog-Melitopol Gas Pipeline'; Status=operating since StartYear1=2024, ConstructionYear=2023/7, corridor Taganrog->Melitopol, straight-line 272.73 km). P5989's own sources describe modernization ('replacement of pipe... doubled pressure, 1.5x volume') of the SAME Taganrog-through-DNR corridor that P7817/P7818 track as a separate 'reconstruction of the retired Soviet Taganrog-Mariupol-Berdyansk pipeline.' Independent UA source united24media.com (Jul 2025) describes 'two pipelines' being built along this stretch -- one Taganrog-Mariupol, another continuing to Berdyansk with Melitopol as the final destination -- which is consistent with P5989 being the SAME physical corridor as P7817+P7818 combined, just tracked under a different name/PID with a different (earlier, 'operating') status. Do not merge unilaterally -- flag for adjudication whether P5989 and P7817/P7818 are the same asset double-counted, or genuinely parallel/successive builds (e.g., P5989 = a faster interim pipe, P7817/P7818 = the slower Soviet-line capital-repair program).
resolutions.researcher_notes: GGIT gas sheet has FOUR rows on this exact geography: P1457 'Taganrog-Mariupol-Berdyansk Gas Pipeline' (retired 2009, dia 1000mm, 516.00 km merged -- this is the original Soviet trunk, matches the gem.wiki infobox for Rostov-Taganrog-Zhdanov). P7817 = its Taganrog-Mariupol reconstruction (construction, 700mm). P7818 (this row) = its Mariupol-Berdyansk reconstruction (proposed, 500mm). P5989 = 'Taganrog-Melitopol-Berdyansk Gas Pipeline' (operating since 2024, no diameter recorded, sourced to TASS 2024-04-29 (tass.ru/obschestvo/20680005 -- 403'd for me directly but content recovered via web search snippet: 'В ДНР впервые не ограничивали потребление газа зимой' -- modernization of the Taganrog-Melitopol section THROUGH DNR, new pipe-laying doubled pressure/1.5x volume, now also supplies gas to Zaporizhzhia) and dan-news.ru 2023-07-27 (verified live, confirms only the two endpoints Taganrog/Melitopol, no diameter/length, no mention of Mariupol or Berdyansk in that specific article). Neither P5989 citation names Mariupol or Berdyansk explicitly, so I cannot mechanically prove P5989 IS the same pipe as P7817/P7818 -- but the geography (Taganrog->Melitopol necessarily transits the Mariupol/Berdyansk coastal corridor) and the independent United24 description of parallel construction along that exact stretch make this a real, non-trivial overlap risk, not a stretch. This is exactly the kind of relabeled/duplicate risk the sweep is designed to catch -- flagging rather than resolving per instructions.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Read the underlying primary document behind the sheet's own Status/Diameter [ref] (archive.org/details/58_20251012 = DNR Ministry of Construction Order No.58-od, 27.03.2025, full OCR text pulled from the item's own djvu.txt derivative). It approves territorial-planning documentation for THREE separate 'kapitalny remont' (capital repair, method = pipe replacement) linear objects: (1) Taganrog-Mariupol Дu700, km 29.0-71.625; (2) an internal Mariupol GRS-1-to-GRS-2 line, Дu700/500, km 0-11.815; and (3) 'Mariupol-Berdyansk Дu500 na uchastke km 0 - km 0.3' -- i.e. THIS row's own citation supports a capital-repair proposal for only the FIRST 300 METERS of the Mariupol-Berdyansk line, not a 68.93 km reconstruction. The underlying planning documentation was originally approved back on 29.05.2020 (pre-invasion; DNR evidently held provisional plans for this corridor years before Russia occupied Mariupol/Berdyansk in 2022) and the 2025 order is a re-confirmation/republication of that 2020 documentation. Diameter=500mm is well-supported (matches 'Дu500' exactly). Status=proposed is a defensible READING of 'documentation approved, repair not yet executed,' but LengthEstimateKm=68.93 (an unsourced straight-line Mariupol-Berdyansk city-distance estimate) is NOT established by this citation -- the only hard evidence is for a 0.3 km stub. This may simply mean GEM is tracking the intended eventual full-route repair using the first-phase approval as evidence of intent (reasonable), but it should be recorded as an inference, not as if the whole 68.93 km were documented. LengthKnownKm is correctly blank ('--').
